Canonical plan v6 U-012 procedure step 3: 'Compute a deterministic mutation diff and hash server-side, display it before approval, and require expected_diff_hash on approve to prevent stale review writes.'
Current worker/services/imports.ts prepareCanonical uses crypto.randomUUID() for new canonical IDs and slug generation with random suffixes.
Canonical plan v6 U-012 escalation_conditions includes 'mutation diff cannot be made deterministic'.
dispositions.rationale: The defect correctly identifies that the canonical plan v6 U-012 procedure step 3 requires a deterministic mutation diff and hash but does not specify the diff algorithm, hash algorithm, normalization strategy, or how to exclude non-deterministic elements (random UUIDs, random slugs) from the diff. The current prepareCanonical function uses crypto.randomUUID() which would cause diff mismatch even for identical data. This is a real plan specification gap: an executor cannot implement the diff deterministically without explicit guidance on what fields to include, what normalization to apply (whitespace, casing, unicode), what hash algorithm to use (sha256 of canonicalized JSON), and how to handle auto-generated IDs (exclude from diff or freeze seed). The defect is valid and requires a canonical plan mutation to specify the exact deterministic diff algorithm.
dispositions.exact_plan_mutation: Add to U-012 procedure step 3: 'The deterministic mutation diff algorithm is: (1) take a JSON snapshot of the canonical row at the exact moment the review DTO is fetched; (2) compute the prospective canonical row from the staging data using the same prepareCanonical logic but with a fixed seed for crypto.randomUUID() and slug suffix generation (seed derived from trace_id); (3) compute structural diff via RFC 6902 (JSON Patch) restricted to whitelisted canonical fields; (4) canonicalize both pre- and post-snapshots via the same JSON canonicalization scheme (sorted keys, UTF-8 NFC, no whitespace); (5) compute sha256 of the canonicalized JSON Patch document as expected_diff_hash; (6) on approve, re-fetch the current canonical row, re-compute the diff against the prospective, and reject if either the current canonical row or the prospective canonical row has changed (stale-diff rejection). Random IDs and slugs are excluded from the diff payload but the seeded pre-computed values are persisted on the import_records row for replay.'
